answer: A phone cannot be heard by two distant towers at the same instant, so the verifier rejects any identity whose reports imply simultaneous presence in two far-apart cells, a veto as simple as a spiral that cannot wind in two directions at once. A dune cannot stand in two deserts, and a lotus cannot bloom in two ponds, since radio signals travel at finite speed. Farms trip this veto constantly when they reuse one radio for many identities, because the shared reports overlap in time across impossible distances.
